It is one of the {{ill|Ou district|Q11073594|qid=Q11073594}} and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was village shrine. It is enshrined southeast of Chausuyama, identified with “Kaminahi-no” of the Oi District section in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|de|Izumo Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記|simple|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|zh|出雲國風土記|qid=Q11395858}}. {{nihongo|'''Manai Shrine'''|真名井神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
It enshrines {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Kami}} and {{ill|Amatsuhikone|fa|آماتسوهیکونه|fr|Amatsuhikone|it|Amatsuhikone|ja|アマツヒコネ|zh|天津日子根命|qid=Q10940228|lt=Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto}}.

== History ==
In the Oi District section of ''Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki'', two shrines are listed: “Manai-sha” (a Shrine Bureau shrine) and “Matsuna-i-sha” (non–Shrine Bureau shrine). The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' also records “Manai Shrine” in Oi District, Izumo Province. It is said that rites of this shrine were handled by the Akigami family, shrine family of {{ill|Kamosu Shrine|fr|Kamosu-jinja|ja|神魂神社|qid=Q3192477}}, who served as both priest and ritual-fire attendant, and that shrine buildings of both shrines were built in the same periods<ref>Asakawa (2006), p.39</ref>.

==Shimane Prefecture designated cultural properties==
*Honden - designated in {{ill|Marcel Hirscher|Q2072|qid=Q2072}}.

== Manai Falls ==
East of this shrine is a waterfall called “Manai Falls”<ref>Regarding Manai, in ancient usage “i” (well) could also mean “waterfall” (Seki (2006), p.189).</ref>. ''Unyōshi'' notes “Manai Kōjin” near this waterfall and identifies that place with the Manai-sha of the Fudoki. Water drawn from this basin is said to have been used from ancient times for the sacred-fire succession rite and Niiname-sai of the {{ill|Izumo clan|Q11395856|qid=Q11395856}}.
